summary: 50 blocking findings. Two were real and both were mine: a graded -v invocation the contract excludes, and a binary-file flag that never cleared. Seven reference claims were refuted by execution again; the rest were missing coverage.

findings.summary: The verifier grades the excluded -v option as though supporting it were required.
findings.rationale: Right, and mine to fix: a case added in the previous revision graded an invocation with -v while the instruction lists six options and no others. The case is removed, and the errata now says plainly that nothing grades -G or -v, so accepting or rejecting them makes no difference to a submission.

gate.rule: a graded invocation may use only options the instruction lists: the -v case is removed, and the errata now says accepting or rejecting -G and -v makes no difference because nothing grades them

findings.summary: The append-command branch never rejects a reversed address range, although the erratum reserves acceptance of reversed ranges for `=`.
findings.rationale: Refuted by execution: on the finding's own script GNU ed 1.19 produces exactly what the reference produces, in standard output, exit status and files. A reversed range is accepted by a, a global substitution whose expression can match empty is refused only when a zero-length match repeats, a backslash-only list line behaves as the errata says, and \<\> compiles. Each script is now a graded case.

findings.summary: Binary-file state is sticky: after a binary file has been read, reading a non-binary replacement file never clears self.isbinary, so a later empty read incorrectly suppresses the normal final newline of that text buffer.
findings.rationale: Right, and mine to fix: the binary flag added in the second revision was never cleared, so after a NUL-holding file every later empty read suppressed the final newline of an ordinary text buffer. Loading a file now sets the flag from that file. Probing around it also exposed ed's 'Newline inserted' path for a read that follows a line with no newline, which the reference now implements, and four cases pin the states.

gate.rule: wrong path sticky-binary-state: reverting the load-time reset of the binary flag must fail test_odd_files, so the state cannot become sticky again
